title: One dither compositor for every picture on the page
summary: Five scenes (hero, two chapters, a glyph interlude, the close) woven by one raw-WebGL context on a detached canvas: each scene draws into the top-left slice of a shared buffer that only grows, then `drawImage`s the slice into its own in-flow 2D canvas in the same task, so pictures scroll natively and sit under their section's text; four clips are pooled (one texture each, uploaded at most once per new frame however many scenes show it), play only while a visible scene shows them, and a scene redraws only on screen and only when a clip frame or one of its settings changed, at 30 fps at most; light sections take normal levels and dark sections inverted ones; the hero develops on arrival, the rest with the scroll; seasons swap by levels, not a cross-fade; a measured single context; stills under reduced motion
variants: Slices copied into in-flow 2D canvases (this, default): native scroll, DOM stacking, any number of scenes
One fixed full-viewport canvas scissored per scene rect (fewer copies, but it trails native touch scroll by a frame)
Per-scene contexts, as many shipped sites do: simplest, but Chromium keeps sixteen live contexts and loses the oldest
